title: Finite pushforward preserves and reflects relative degreewise pseudo-coherence
statement: Let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be locally finite type morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], and let $\pi:X\to Y$ be a finite $S$-morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $m\in\mathbf Z$ and let $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ have quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves [def-pc-derived-category, pqf-def-coherent]. Then $K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex] if and only if $R\pi_*K\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$. There is no Noetherian or global cohomological boundedness assumption.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $\pi$ is affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Thus [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh] applies to the given unbounded $K$, and $L=R\pi_*K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology.

source.place: Tag 09UK, first observation in the proof; Tag 08D5(1)

proof.text: Choose an affine cover $S=\bigcup_i V_i$, and for each $i$ an affine open cover of the inverse image of $V_i$ in $Y$ by $W_{ij}$. Set $U_{ij}=\pi^{-1}(W_{ij})$. These are affine opens covering the inverse image of $V_i$ in $X$, since $\pi$ is affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For one pair write $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $W_{ij}=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U_{ij}=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The two given locally finite type structural maps make $A$ and $B$ finite type $R$-algebras by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], and finiteness of $\pi$ says precisely that $B$ is a finite $A$-module. All three ring maps are induced by the given $S$-morphisms, hence form a compatible tower.

source.place: Tag 09UK, affine reduction and finite-algebra translation

proof.text:
Put $M=R\Gamma(U_{ij},K|_{U_{ij}})\in D(B)$, using module-valued sections as in [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence]. Let $\pi_{ij}:U_{ij}\to W_{ij}$. The open restriction comparison [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open] identifies $L|_{W_{ij}}$ with $R\pi_{ij,*}(K|_{U_{ij}})$. Write $p_U:(U_{ij},\mathcal O)\to(\{*\},B)$ and $p_W:(W_{ij},\mathcal O)\to(\{*\},A)$ for the global-section maps, and $h:(\{*\},B)\to(\{*\},A)$ for $A\to B$. Their composites satisfy $p_W\pi_{ij}=h p_U$. Twice applying [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image-composition] therefore gives in $D(A)$
$$R\Gamma(W_{ij},L|_{W_{ij}})\cong Rh_*Rp_{U,*}(K|_{U_{ij}})=\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B}M.$$
Indeed [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image] on the one-point map $h$ is scalar restriction; it is exact because it keeps the underlying groups, so its derived functor is termwise restriction. This proves the comparison with its $A$-action, not merely after forgetting to abelian groups.

source.place: Tag 09UK, derived affine translation; cohomology.tex Tag 0D5T

proof.text: Suppose first $K$ is relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent. Clause (3) of [lem-sfb-relative-m-pseudocoherence-derived-sections] says that each $M$ above is relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent over $R$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-algebra-relative-m-pseudocoherence] to $R\to A\to B$: its finite-type and module-finiteness hypotheses were checked in step 2. The comparison in step 3 makes $R\Gamma(W_{ij},L|_{W_{ij}})$ relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent over $R$. Clause (2) of the affine-section criterion on the chosen covers of $S$ and $Y$ proves the assertion for $L$. Conversely, start with the relative property for $L$, use clause (3) on each $W_{ij}$, the same comparison and the reverse implication of the finite-algebra lemma to get the property for each $M$, and then use clause (2) on the chosen covers of $S$ and $X$ to obtain it for $K$. Relative pseudo-coherence is invariant under the comparison isomorphism: compose a finite-free approximation with that isomorphism in its defining condition [def-sfb-ring-relative-m-pseudocoherent]. The argument fixes an arbitrary $m$ and never uses a global cohomological bound.
